findings.reason: §3's decision (what a mention costs) and its done-whens are moot at HEAD because a mention already costs zero (the decision's own "nothing at all" option), so the plan should either be retargeted at the residual gap (provenance in the refusal, §4's opt-out) or withdrawn, and leaving it as written would ship a second, parallel notion of mention cost.
findings.text: §1 asserts the estimator "counts every resolvable repository path named anywhere in a node's brief at full file load", and §3 proposes to stop charging a mention at full load and charge it at a reference cost; but `_declared_input_files` (added in `318ec2b6a`, ancestor of the plan's own evidence revision `1135b00d9`) already charges a path only when its clause declares it an input and charges a mere mention at nothing, and `_paths_a_clause_charges` already withholds the paths a negation governs, so the "brief prose is priced at full load" premise and all of §3 describe a defect that was removed before the plan was revised

findings.reason: the section is nearly complete in the tree; the honest node is one clause (name each contributor's provenance within the existing renderer), not the new reporting path §2 specifies.
findings.text: §2's premise that "it reports only the total" is false: `_context_refusal_detail` already renders "largest contributing files: <path> (<n> tokens), …" into the refusal `detail`, built by `_context_contributors` from the same `write_paths`/`named_files` groups, so the §2 done-when is already met except for the one clause that says whether the term arrived as a declared write path or a mention

findings.reason: a §2/§8 that names `_context_contributors` and `_context_refusal_detail` as the owner to extend is a one-clause change versus a new subsystem, and the plan's own §8 already lives in routing.py where the owner sits.
findings.text: §2/§8 propose to compute and report a per-file term breakdown beside the total, but `_context_contributors` already builds exactly that ranked per-file list from `repository_files.write_paths` and `repository_files.named_files` (each record already carries `estimated_tokens` and a group that is the write-path/mention distinction), so a new breakdown forks the owner; the section-8 evidence grep (`per_file`/`per-file`) missed it only because the existing identifiers are `write_paths`/`named_files`

findings.reason: §7 asks to add a plan-level figures directory the node does not need because it already holds a figures path under its own fragment; the real question is whether a node's own `<node-id>` figure directory satisfies the graphics mandate, which is the opposite of the change §7 specifies — and §7's asserted "measured" conflict must be re-checked against the per-node grant that exists at HEAD.
findings.text: §7 states that `_grant_landing_write_paths` gives every node "the cumulative evidence record and the plan file" and that `docs/figures/<plan>/` is absent from the set; neither is the current design: `_grant_landing_write_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2052) grants the node's own disjoint fragment `docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html` and `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/` via `_landing_fragment_paths` (dispatch.py:2014), while the cumulative record, the plan file and the `docs/figures/<plan>` topic are owned by `_shared_landing_paths` (dispatch.py:1963), and the prompt (reckon/crew/prompts.py:167) already directs each worker to `docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/`

findings.reason: extending one renderer keeps one owner of the refusal text, where a second reporting path beside `_context_refusal_detail` is the drift the plan objects to elsewhere; the section should be rewritten as a one-clause extension of the owner.
findings.text: the section adds a report of the dominant term rather than extending `_context_refusal_detail`, which already renders the ranked contributors, and it gives no reason the existing renderer cannot carry the one missing fact (contributor provenance)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan adds no new module; it edits branches inside `reckon/crew/routing.py` and `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`, and its §4/§5 fields are carried on existing records rather than spread across new wrappers, so it does not add surface; the depth defect it does carry is reported under duplicate_owner, where it re-derives an existing breakdown.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2/§8 re-derive the per-file breakdown already owned by `_context_contributors` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3319) and already surfaced by `_context_refusal_detail`, and §7 restates the landing placement already owned by `_shared_landing_paths`/`_landing_fragment_paths` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1963, :2014).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan does not cite that `_declared_input_files` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3098) already stopped charging mere mentions at file load, nor that `_context_refusal_detail` (reckon/crew/routing.py:3353) already reports the dominant contributors, so the premise of §1 and much of §2/§3 is already in the tree.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 proposes a new dominant-term report beside `_context_refusal_detail`, which already renders the largest contributing files with token figures, and the plan nowhere says why that existing renderer cannot be extended.
